home.title: Welcome to Vite - NestJS - Turbo Boilerplate

about.title: A starter stack for full-stack authentication flows
about.description: This workspace combines a Vite React frontend, a NestJS backend, shared DTO contracts, and Prisma-backed persistence so teams can start from a coherent baseline instead of wiring the same pieces together again.

sections.title: What is already included
body: The frontend talks to the backend through a shared DTO package, which keeps request and response shapes aligned across workspaces.
The backend ships with authentication, Swagger, Prisma integration, and a health endpoint, giving you the core plumbing needed to stand up a product quickly.

sections.title: How teams usually extend it
body: Treat the apps directory as your delivery surface and the packages directory as the reusable contract and data layer.
Once the infrastructure is running, you can add feature modules, expand the Prisma schema, and evolve shared DTOs without duplicating validation logic between frontend and backend.

cta.title: Use the starter as a baseline, not a finished product
cta.body: Create an account to test the auth flow, then replace this copy and the legal pages with your own product content before shipping.

contact.title: Route support and ownership through maintainers you can actually reach
contact.description: This starter does not embed a production support channel. The safest default is to direct contributors to your repository issue tracker and replace this page with your real support contact before launch.

sections.title: Recommended channel today
body: Use the repository issue tracker for bug reports, integration questions, and setup problems while the project is still in template form.
If you fork this starter for a real product, update this page with a support email, an SLA expectation, and a clear escalation path for urgent incidents.

sections.title: What to document before production
body: List who owns billing, privacy, and technical support so users do not have to guess where to ask.
If the product serves different regions, document language support and business hours here instead of hiding them inside a README.

cta.title: Want to test the app instead of the template?
cta.body: Create a local account and walk through the auth flow while you shape your own support process around the product.

imprint.title: This page is a starter placeholder for company disclosure
imprint.description: An imprint or company disclosure page is often mandatory in some regions, but the required content depends on the operator, jurisdiction, and business model. The template can give you a route, but it cannot supply legally correct business details for you.

sections.title: What is missing by design
body: No company name, registered address, legal representative, or registration data is shipped with this repository because those values must come from the organization operating the product.
If you deploy this starter publicly, replace this placeholder with verified company information before you invite users to rely on it.

sections.title: Suggested next step
body: Ask legal or operations to provide the exact disclosure text required for the countries where you operate.
Keep the final copy versioned in the repository so changes to business ownership and addresses are reviewed like any other production change.

cta.title: Keep the route, replace the details
cta.body: The point of this page is to stop sending users into a dead link while making the follow-up work obvious.

privacy.title: Privacy content needs a real policy before deployment
privacy.description: The codebase demonstrates cookies, authentication, and persistence, which means any real deployment needs a privacy policy that reflects actual data handling. This placeholder keeps navigation honest while making the gap explicit.

sections.title: What the starter currently implies
body: Authentication uses cookies and backend persistence, so users will reasonably expect clear disclosure about what data is stored, how long it is retained, and who can access it.
Because deployment details vary by team, this repository does not claim a retention policy, subprocessors, or regional compliance posture that may not be true for your fork.

sections.title: Before you go live
body: Document your data categories, legal basis, retention windows, and contact method for privacy requests.
Review frontend analytics, session storage, and backend logging as part of the same pass so the written policy matches the software.

cta.title: Exercise the flow, then add your policy
cta.body: You can use the auth starter now, but the legal copy still needs owner-supplied content before a public release.

terms.title: Terms of service should describe your actual product obligations
terms.description: A template can reserve the route and give teams a place to land, but acceptable use rules, warranties, billing terms, and account enforcement policies depend on the service you run.

sections.title: Why this is still useful
body: Users no longer hit a dead link when they look for your terms, which is better than hiding the absence of legal content behind broken navigation.
The copy here makes it clear that the route exists for product completeness, not because the repository ships a production-ready legal agreement.

sections.title: What to replace before release
body: Define account rules, service limitations, ownership of user content, and how termination works.
If you charge money, add billing, refunds, and renewal language that matches the systems you actually operate.

cta.title: Use the app flow while the policy work catches up
cta.body: You can still validate routing and authentication now, then swap in approved legal copy later as part of launch readiness.
